items.title: Core suites, the require rule, and spirit as the one door
items.box:
Core suites, the require rule, and spirit as the one door. From goal/G38.2, as discussed there so far.

Decided (Andy, 2026-10-24):
- Two kinds of suites. Core suites assert the current design of SpiritOS, permanently. Task suites assert that one assigned task is done.
- Core suites sit in a test folder that is always a child of the folder holding the code they test. They are part of the product: they need design approval, are never written ad hoc, and deskVerify runs them as a category of their own, as one bundle, the core verification of SpiritOS's design and design intent.
- Core suites carry scope-limited, configurable stack-frame tests and dependency-rule assertions, equally configurable.
- The require rule: a require path that starts with ../ may only add a file name, never descend into a subfolder of an ancestor; any other require path starts with <module>/, the module's own children. A sibling in the module's own folder is legal ("\"siblings\" should be legal in a require statement"). So a module requires its own children, its siblings, or its ancestors' scripts.
- A scan of every .js file reports each require that breaks the rule to deskVerify as a failure: "require error: process/js/desk/desk.js".
- spirit.js sits at the run root, spirit/run/spirit.js, the node's root of its own fs scope (Andy: "NOT repo-root. i meant in the run-root, the nodes root of its own fs scope"). Every module first makes sure spirit is a plain global in its scope, and reaches other modules through the spirit object, the official spirit toolset, never by a require path. kernel.js stays where it is and goes once the cleanup is finished; the spirit object is then the door to all legal functionality ("i know it's a long goal, but worth it, i think."). index.html goes the same way as kernel.js (Andy: "index.html will deprecate like kernel.js").
- spirit.js is the first thing loaded by face.html and by every module that is not the node server or a relay server; those two build spirit themselves and are its embodiments (Andy: "it needs to be the first thing loaded by face.html or or any module the is not a relay-server or a node-server, those are the actual embodyments of spirit.js?").
- From this, normal goals follow, such as "move all sub-components of peerPost.js into subfolder peerPost/".
- deskAgent moves from a Levant node to Andy's own node, with a code-reviewing agent that does the API part of verification, code review included.

The tree today (36123dfe):
- 33 files under run/ break the require rule, 88 requires, each reaching into a subfolder of an ancestor or of another module. The test files break it about 1,200 times in 437 files, each reaching into run/js/.
- Two spirits: kernel.js builds one (spirit.core and the node's tools; server.js requires it, the browser gets it as window.spirit). face/spirit.js builds the other, the object of verbs, and the shell adds spirit.elements and spirit.data to it.

Recommended:
- The require scan as one more rule of the stack-frame checks plugin, which already scans code and reports to deskVerify.
- Shedding: a task suite leaves when its goal closes, unless a design promotes it to core.

Open:
- Andy's further rules for the design, among them the re-placing of code modules in the tree (not their function).

- 1. spirit.js at the repo root, one object holding today's spirit (face/spirit.js), which every module may reach with ancestors plus a file name. The face keeps getting it inline, read from the root now.

- 3. Then one item per module or folder: it takes what it uses from spirit, and its breaks go to zero. peerPost into peerPost/ is one such.
- 4. Last: kernel.js goes, once nothing reaches it but spirit.
- Core suites run beside this as items of their own.
- Cost of the repo root, so it is not hidden: three tools copy only the spirit/ folder into a node (the suites' fake nodes and two installers), and the face reads spirit.js from inside the node's tree today. Each gets taught the root in item 1.

items.title: Move spirit.js to spirit/run/
items.creator: claude-windows
items.box:
Move spirit.js to spirit/run/ (goal/G40), and make it the one spirit object every script installs first. Everything it brings with it, end to end (Andy, 2026-10-24).

DECIDED
The move
- spirit/run/face/spirit.js becomes spirit/run/spirit.js by git mv, history kept; nothing stays at the old path.
- It stays core: coreFiles.js names it (today it is core only as part of face/). The static route serves /spirit.js; /face/spirit.js answers 404.
- Its loaders follow: serveCommon.inlineSpirit (face.html, relay and home node, as its first script); index.html (deprecated like kernel.js, works until it goes); face/shell.js; appServer.js; the server scripts, by ../../spirit.js: chatClerver, desk, commitCheck, deskAgentEar, removeAgent, deskAgent, deskClient, publishData, fileServer, relayLimits. The 17 family api.js comments that name the old path are corrected.
The spirit object, the same in a face and in node
- Has today: the static helpers (error, formatBytes, escapeHtml, check, field rules) and families loaded when first called (createSpirit, forNode).
- Gains: in node it installs itself as the global spirit, as on a page.
- Gains, in this item, what scripts outside the node and the relay take from kernel.js today, under the kernel's own names, so no call in them changes: the job calls (spirit.core.jobs.publish, start, progress, end), the node's constants and version (spirit.core.node.const, spirit.core.const.VERSION), the MIME types (spirit.core.const.MIME_TYPES, a table of its own; kernel.js keeps its table, which goes when kernel.js goes: Andy, "kernel can keep its MIME table, that will go when kernel goes.") and peerPost. Each such script then drops its kernel.js require and its local spirit, with no rename (Q1, cleared): appServer.js, introSpector.js (appServer loads it), chatClerver, desk, deskAgent, deskClient, deskVerify, fileServer.
- Gains spirit.require(path, key) -> Promise, in spirit.js itself, so any component touched later loads its own: path from the run root; key null or left out for the owner's node, else a peer's ID key as it is.
- A path ending <name>/<name>.family/api.js or js/<name>/api.js is an interface, bound as spirit.<name> through api {family}; with a key, asked of that peer over peerPost (forPeer). Any other path is a component: required in node, fetched through the link and run on a face.
- spirit.fs, at its end, loads fs: no script outside the node and the relay reaches fs another way.
Every script that depends on it
- Installs spirit as a global in its first statement, then uses spirit.<member>, never a local copy (10 server scripts hold it as spiritObject today).
- server.js and relayServer.js are spirit's embodiments: they build it and load no spirit.js. Modules only the node or the relay loads (serveCommon, relay.js, relayRequest.js, apiAuth, hub and the like) are the embodiment too and keep kernel.js.
Removed
- process/js/imageStats/ and process/js/wordpressScanner/ leave the repo; serveCommon.js, pushOrigin.js and the suites jobsSearch, moduleIds, pushOrigin, servableAssets stop naming them. Design notes are records and stay.
- keyTail goes wherever it is used: kernel.js, apiAuth, hub, serveCommon, desk, the deskAgentRemote and natterDetails panes, and the suites that name it (keyTail.js among them). No key's tail is shown anywhere any more (Andy, 2026-10-24, to Q2): the contact row's tail field and every caption or label built from a tail go with it.

FILES AND GRANTS (counted at 36123dfe)
- The item's list is exactly what changes: 73 files, 23 of them core; 1 new (spirit/run/spirit.js); 6 deleted (imageStats/ and wordpressScanner/, their scripts, manifests and package files); 26 suites, the new red to be added with it.
- Granted: G1, G2 and G3. G3 also covers server.js, jobs.js, js/client/shell.js and shell/js/fileViewer.js, which this item does not touch: they only read the MIME table, which keeps its name.
- Suites corrected for the path: spiritObject, spiritServers, appsApp, deskClientNext, deskTables, testSupport.

THE RED
- spirit.js at the run root, the old path gone, nothing in run/ or test/ names it; it is core.
- face.html from home and from a relay carries it inline first; index.html loads /spirit.js; /face/spirit.js 404.
- Every server script that loads it starts, installs spirit first and holds no local copy; every app server still starts and reports its job through spirit; none but the node and the relay requires kernel.js.
- spirit.require: a component and an interface in node and on a face (spirit.require('process/js/desk/desk.family/api.js') gives spirit.desk), and a peer's family by key.
- The two removed scripts and keyTail are gone.

END TO END
- Relays updated, restarted, tree tagged (capacity, history row, commit, tag; Andy's word before the tag), in the same step as the nodes: an old relay serves face.html with no spirit object, and inlineSpirit logs when it finds none.
- Andy's node and the agents' nodes restarted right after their pull (a running node breaks the moment the file moves).
- Regression by hand, shell at home and face through a relay: log in, open an app, save an icon, open Desk. Old reds may stay red. A browser holding an old index.html gets 404 until it reloads.

- An app server's interface sits at process/js/<name>/<name>.family/api.js, a node family's at js/<name>/api.js; the node finds them by those paths when it answers api {family}.

- One catch: a key in base64 holds / characters (yours: ...uOYQFtJM/kr1b+76Fj...), so a path cannot tell where the key ends.
- Plainest fix: the key is written in base64url in the path (- and _ for + and /), which spirit turns back; nothing else changes.

all: proposed solutions for the path issue with fetching api's from peers?

cw, four ways, best first:
- A. The peer apart from the path: spirit.require('process/js/desk/desk.family/api.js', { peer: key }). The path means the same at home and at a peer, the key is never parsed out of a string, nothing is encoded. Recommended.
- B. The key in base64url in the path (- and _ for + and /), turned back by spirit: one string, but every key written by hand has to be converted first.
- C. The key by its fixed length: an ed25519 key in base64 is always 60 characters, so the path is the first 60 characters and the rest. No conversion, but a rule nobody can see when reading the path.
- D. The peer by its contact name ('@bert/desk'): readable, but a label is not an identity (decision 0001-era, "labels are not identities"), so two contacts with one name would ask the wrong node. Not advised.

- wsl: plainest, the key as it is with a mark base64 never holds: spirit.require('desk@<key>'), split at the @, so the key is pasted unchanged and nothing converts it.
- Also works today: every node key is an ed25519 key, 60 characters starting MCowBQYDK2VwAyEA, so a path starting with one can be cut at 60; brittle if the key type ever changes.
- ? @ or base64url?
can the key not simply be a second argument in spirit.require(), by default it's null (owner node) otherwise it's a peer ID?
